## Meteorites

Where have they all landed?

#### Load Libraries

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(maps)
library(mapdata)
library(mapproj)
library(tidytuesdayR)
library(ggstar)
```

#### Load Data

```{r}
meteorites <- readr::read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2019/2019-06-11/meteorites.csv") |>
 filter(year %in% 2000:2005) |>
  tidyr::drop_na()

glimpse(meteorites)
```

map_data() — World

```{r}
world <- map_data("world")

head(world)
```

#### Map of the World

```{r}
ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(data = world,
               aes(x = long, y = lat,
                   group = group,
                   fill = region),
               color = "black") +
  guides(fill = "none") #get rid of legend, because that would be too much
```

#### Mapping Meteorites

```{r}
#| label: fig-meteorites
#| echo: true
#| fig-cap: Fallen Meteorites 2000-2005

ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(data = world,
               aes(x = long, y = lat,
                   group = group,
                   fill="pink"),
               color = "white") +
  guides(fill = "none") +#get rid of legend, because that would be too much
  geom_star(data = meteorites, size=1,
             aes(x = long, y = lat,
                 color = mass)) +
  coord_map() +
  theme_void() +
  coord_map(projection = "mercator",
            xlim = c(-180, 180))+
  theme(panel.background =
          element_rect(fill = "lightblue")) +
  labs(title="Fallen Meteorites 2000-2005",
       color="Mass")


ggsave(here("Week_7", "output", "Meteorites_HW.pdf")) #saves most recent plot by default
```

In @fig-meteorites we can observe fallen meteorites world wide according to their mass.
